concepts.def: Brief store for raw sensory data, under 2 seconds.
Turning information into a usable memory trace.
How much information a store can hold.

walkthroughs.body_html: Information enters the sensory register. Attention moves it to STM. Rehearsal transfers it to LTM. Each store differs in capacity, duration and encoding — STM is acoustic, LTM is semantic.

walkthroughs.h2: Miller's magic number and Peterson duration
walkthroughs.body_html: Miller (1956) found STM capacity is around 7±2 chunks. Peterson & Peterson (1959) found that without rehearsal, STM fades in around 18-30 seconds. Chunking groups items together to overcome the limit.

Sensation is raw input from the eyes and ears. Perception is the brain's interpretation. Perception can be shaped by expectation, culture and context, which is why two people may see the same scene differently.
